correctness.rationale: For every term the forced-one consequent-coordinate induction is valid. Conversely each Boolean f that is one on p_i=1 has form p_i OR g and is represented by the displayed explicit recursive implication translation; every case is checked at p_i=0,1. For a desired set E containing a positive two-coordinate face, the explicit four-case pair of forced-one functions yields equality exactly E. This proves both inclusions and hence all arities, with cardinality m from 2^{k-2} to 2^k, sharp lower witness p1=(p1->p2). One-variable cases are separately evaluated; bit-conjugation/reversal preserves equation solutions. A standalone independently constructed truth-table closure checker exhaustively verifies term functions and equalizers through k=3 but is not relied on for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Cardó 2026 explicitly leaves the spectra of these four two-element binary operations undetermined. Fournier et al. 2012 identify the clone of individual implicational term functions but do not state the stronger exact family of equality sets between two formulas, or its arity-wise and all-arity agreement spectra. The new four-case equality-set argument closes the missing comparison. Searches across published research records and primary/related literature exposed no equivalent characterization; an older unpublished/poorly indexed observation remains a real priority risk. This is self-review, not proof of worldwide novelty.
residual_risks: Known 2012 clone description makes the new equalizer result accessible to earlier researchers; an unindexed older equational-probability argument may exist.
Semantic research-record searches and accessible papers are not an exhaustive priority audit; inability to prove absence of older observations is explicit.
The 2026 table is a preprint and could be superseded by a newer version or another author independently resolving the same spectra.

value.rationale: The recent motivating work explicitly identifies a missing exact invariant for four fundamental two-element binary operations. The new theorem solves that gap exactly (all dyadic fractions at least 1/4), including a complete description of which valuation sets can solve one equation. The 1/4 obstruction, all-arity spectrum and full equalizer geometry quantify expressive limitation in the smallest nontrivial implicational language, a natural mathematical object. Known term-clone description alone did not make the sharp face-geometry classification part of existing literature. No generalization to many-valued or biased semantics is asserted.
